data.title: Griseofulvin
data.summary: III Antifungals · Benzofuran fungistatic antibiotic (from Penicillium griseofulvum)
data.body:
_Oral · III Antifungals_

**Class:** Benzofuran fungistatic antibiotic (from Penicillium griseofulvum)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds microtubule proteins (tubulin) and disrupts the mitotic spindle → arrests fungal cell division in metaphase
- Deposited in keratin precursor cells, so new keratin resists infection
- Active only against dermatophytes; no effect on Candida, Malassezia or deep fungi

## Pharmacokinetics
- Poorly water-soluble; absorption improves with a fatty meal and with smaller particle size
- Microsize and ultramicrosize forms are not interchangeable mg-for-mg (ultramicrosize is better absorbed)
- Half-life 9–24 h; reaches the stratum corneum through sweat; washes out quickly after stopping
- Metabolised in the liver; a CYP inducer

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Tinea capitis — especially Microsporum infections (first choice), and children
- Extensive tinea corporis/cruris when other drugs are unavailable
- Not suitable for onychomycosis (needs 12–18 months, poor cure)
- Rarely used for anti-inflammatory purposes (lichen planus, etc.)

## Dose & formulations
- Children (tinea capitis): microsize 20–25 mg/kg/day, or ultramicrosize 10–15 mg/kg/day, with fatty food, for at least 6–8 weeks
- Adults: microsize 500 mg–1 g/day (ultramicrosize 375–750 mg/day)
- Tinea corporis: 2–4 weeks; tinea pedis: 4–8 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Headache (most common; often settles)
- GI upset, taste disturbance
- Photosensitivity; can precipitate or worsen lupus erythematosus and acute porphyria
- Urticaria, morbilliform rash, fixed drug eruption, rarely SJS/TEN
- Hepatotoxicity, leukopenia, proteinuria (rare)
- Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy; men should not father children during treatment and for 6 months after
- Porphyria, hepatic failure, systemic lupus

## Drug interactions
- Enzyme inducer: reduces efficacy of oral contraceptives, warfarin, cyclosporine
- Phenobarbital reduces griseofulvin absorption
- Alcohol: disulfiram-like reaction

## Monitoring
- CBC and LFT only for prolonged courses
- Advise extra contraception

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category X) — teratogenic and embryotoxic.

## Viva points
- Fungistatic; acts on the mitotic spindle
- Drug of choice for Microsporum tinea capitis; terbinafine is better for Trichophyton tonsurans
- Give with a fatty meal (e.g. milk)
- Ineffective against Candida and Malassezia
- Enzyme inducer — reduces oral contraceptive efficacy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.10 (Systemic antifungal agents), Table 10.5; Khopkar ch.2. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
